The 2027 Alliance Aurum 38FB Is the Most Beautiful Fifth Wheel RV, Hands Down
38 photos
Photo: Alliance RV
With all the new and innovative releases announced for 2027 from all the major RV players and even some we have never heard of before, it does feel like we're at a turning point in the industry. Alliance RV wants to make sure we know that the surprises are far from over and that they saved the best for last.
They call it the Aurum, the new golden standard in the RV industry and the "new definition of luxury." Aurum is a brand-new, built-from-the-ground-up series of luxury fifth wheels with the Alliance RV badge, designed over the course of two full years and engineered to be different in absolutely every aspect imaginable.
The Alliance Aurum series will include several floorplans , but their exact number or planned release date have not yet been made public. Instead, Alliance is choosing to offer a first taste of it through the introduction of the first completed unit of the Aurum 38FB floorplan, which you can see toured in the video at the bottom of the page. It is, hands down, the most beautiful, elegant, and luxurious fifth wheel RV ever, with the only exception of fully custom rigs.
The Aurum 38FB is a front bathroom floorplan, with a rear living, a middle kitchen, and the bedroom on the upper deck. The layout is common to fifth wheels, but the execution is anything but: Alliance set out to create something different and very sophisticated, and they achieved just that.
Photo: Alliance RV The RV comes in at 41 feet 2 inches (12.5 meters) of length and is built on a 101-inch (256-cm) widebody chassis that Alliance built in-house and named the Fortis. It's engineered to work as one integrated structural system, with 17-inch (43-cm) stacked tube construction and an interlocked Z-beam design, so that it offers more structural strength and better handling, but also a completely unobstructed front basement that's accessible through four different points.
The chassis is a tandem axle dual-wheel one with MORryde independent suspension, hydraulic disc brakes, 17.5-inch H-rated tires, and TPMS. Standard equipment on the outside includes 6-point hydraulic auto-leveling, rear and side camera system with monitor, and a seamless A.R.M.O.R. spray-on roof with one-piece fiberglass caps at the front and rear. The rear one features striking automotive styling.
The sidewalls are 3.5-inch thick, the thickest in the industry . Combined with an upgraded HVAC system, which is also an industry first, and the double-pane argon gas-filled windows, Alliance promises a rolling home – palace, better said – that will remain comfortable throughout the year, fully insulated, and durable.
Photo: Alliance RV While having "only" three slide-outs, the widebody chassis and the smart design allow Alliance to build inside a real home on wheels, of the finest kind. That's not an exaggeration, either: this fifth wheel features stuff you won't find anywhere else, from the GE Cafe appliances (the kind you'll normally find in premium park tiny houses ) to the Italian leather sofa and theater seats, hardwood furniture, and the oversize square windows with built-in sliding blackouts and flyscreens.
As Alliance puts it, this fifth wheel "imagines what a premium fifth wheel can be through thoughtful design, elevated comfort, and an uncompromising approach to the RV experience." Again, not empty words because they're backed by the final product.
This fifth wheel offers sleeping for as many as four people, if you decide to use the living room pull-out sofa as a secondary bedroom. It has two bathrooms, one of which is a half-bath because it doesn't have a shower and the other is a spa-like ensuite complete with a dedicated laundry station (a proper one, not just a washer-dryer closet).
Photo: Alliance RV It has a complete gourmet kitchen where neither functionality nor space is lacking, offering a waterfall island, a full coffee station, a large pantry, and oversize GE appliances, including a dishwasher. It comes with a modular dining space that will adapt to your needs, whether you need a breakfast bar or a dining table for four.
It has a full entertainment lounge with hidden storage behind the entertainment wall and extra nice stuff like hidden cup holders and electric recline function on the premium theater seats.
The Aurum 38FB is specced to be one notch above the rest, with three 15,000-BTU Chill Cube AC units with heat pumps (a fourth is optional), a 40,000-BTU furnace for the house and a separate 25,000-BTU one for the underbelly, a 60,000-BTU on-demand tankless water heater, and 80 lb (36 kg) of propane in total.
Photo: Alliance RV It also comes standard with a Victron energy system with 800W of solar on the roof, a 3000W inverter, and a 400Ah lithium battery. It features ample storage, including a MORryde slide-out tray in that giant basement, several separate exterior bays, an outdoor TV in a dedicated compartment, two Girard legless awnings, and large holding tanks – 98 gallons (371 liters) for freshwater, 106 gallons (401 liters) for gray, and 106 gallons more for black water.
Full automotive bodypaint is included standard, with five options in total to choose from, Tuxedo, Platinum, Executive, Black Label, and Reserve. The unit shown below is in Black Label, a gorgeous, striking matte black that would stand out on its own, even without everything else.
Options include a 60kW NPS generator, a SolarMax+ upgrade on the solar array that will get you full autonomy from the grid, slide toppers, a queen bed instead of the tilting king bed, and a MORryde GooseTech gooseneck box.
Photo: Alliance RV Alliance mentions an empty weight of 20,010 lbs (9,076 kg) and a gross weight of 24,000 lbs (10,886 kg), and a starting MSRP of $269,048. The Aurum 38FB will be produced in just 365 units, and the one below is the first of that series, so that adds to the premium pricing.
